question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Chebyshev distance is defined as

$$
{d}_{\infty }(a,b)=‖a-b{‖}_{\infty }
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $v,$

$$
‖v{‖}_{\infty }=max(|{v}_{1}|,|{v}_{2}|,…,|{v}_{N}|).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{\infty }(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{\infty } \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]‖}_{\infty } \\  & =max(|2-(-3)|,|-7-(-1)|,|1-5|) \\  & =max(5,6,4) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
